study type: Protocol design for a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
outcome: Food allergen sensitization (egg, milk, peanut) at 12 months of age
cohort: Pregnant women and their newborns, where newborns are at high risk for allergies due to a first-degree relative with atopic disease, including 40 infants born vaginally and 80 infants born by cesarean delivery.
finding: This pilot study aims to evaluate the effects of vaginal seeding in cesarean-delivered infants on food allergen sensitization, microbiome, and immune responses.
mod_finding: The study investigates whether vaginal seeding can partially restore the microbiota of infants born by cesarean delivery and reduce the risk of food allergen sensitization.
